messages.author: 9c58a88e8518854a
messages.subject: gl.report.heterozygosity loci number don't tally
parts:
Hello team, 
I am doing some diversity studies and I used the function gl.report.heterozygosity in dartR and the summary results looks like below: 
pop nInd nLoc polyLoc monoLoc all_NALoc Ho HoSD He HeSD uHe uHeSD FIS
Pop1 41.40211 5787 1742 4045 0 0.044541 0.115963 0.076586 0.153783 0.077523 0.155663 0.425442
Pop2 63.43045 5787 1729 4058 0 0.021018 0.055712 0.041448 0.099718 0.041777 0.10051 0.496905
Pop3 9.962094 2770 3531 2256 3017 0.014524 0.079478 0.05754 0.137695 0.06058 0.144971 0.760249
Pop4 25.958 3833 2482 3305 1954 0.034027 0.140141 0.030283 0.108032 0.030878 0.110154 -0.10199
The part I have highlighted shows some discrepancies where the monomorphic and polymorphic loci for pop3 and 4 does not add up to the total number of loci. What could be the problem?
I know this is no poppr forum but may be I can get help too; When I try to do AMOVA with genalex data from dartR it gives this error (Error in eigen(delta, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE) : 
  infinite or missing values in 'x'
In addition: Warning message: 
In is.euclid(xdist) : Zero distance(s))
Kindly assist, 
regards, 
Kimani

messages.author: 12c1b48ba80ae340
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.report.heterozygosity loci number don't tally
parts:
Hi Kimani,
I can give a partial answer to your questions.
The discrepancy is due to the all_NA loci. The number of loci “nLoc” is calculated excluding them. So 3531+2256-3017 (all_NA) = 2770 (nLoc). 
As for the AMOVA, I would probably remove the NA loci and try again.

Cheers,
Manuela

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.report.heterozygosity loci number don't tally
parts:
Hi Kimani,

I guess that you are using the function gl2genalex to export a genlight object to genalex format. 

The issue might be due to the following:

In the CRAN version of dartR (i.e.install.packages('dartR')), the individuals are exported in the same order as in the genlight object. However, Genalex requires that individuals be ordered by population. This issue has been fixed in the developing of version of dartR (i.e. devtools::install_github('green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev'). 

You could also use the function gl.impute for imputing missing data. We recommend filtering on missing data (i.e. gl.filter.callrate) using a threshold of at least 0.5 before imputation. Also, it is important to read the function documentation of gl.impute and consider what the consequences of imputation would be in downstream analyses, taking into account that imputation is not 100% accurate. 

Cheers,
Luis
